en: Acem Baba is a poet who feels himself close to
in terms of his outlook on life. In his poem, he makes it clear that they do not care about the peasants’ disapproval of such a lifestyle.

zh: 科莱拉人身份是一种不遵从精英建制所开药方的城市身份；它是一种有自身惯例的另类城市性。建制把标准方言规定为成为城市居民的先决条件；而在科莱拉，取代标准方言的是科莱拉俚语。正如在伊斯坦布尔，不能说标准方言的迁入者被视为农民，在科莱拉，不能说科莱拉俚语的人也被视为农民。
en: The Kolerite identity is an urban identity that does not follow the prescriptions dictated by the elite establishment; it is an alternative urbanity which has its own conventions. The standard dialect prescribed by the establishment as a prerequisite of being an urbanite is replaced with Kolerite slang in Kolera. Just as migrants in Istanbul who cannot speak in the standard dialect are regarded as peasants, those who cannot speak Kolerite slang are regarded as peasants in Kolera.

zh: 阿克通奇强调，“一种语言最丰厚的俚语宝藏，在使用这种语言的大都市中诞生并成长”（2015，383）。小说强调科莱拉俚语是一种城市语言，这暗示着科莱拉人的城市性，而且是一种另类城市性。科莱拉人把决定谁是城市居民、谁不是城市居民的权力，从精英霸权手中夺回：能否成为城市居民，取决于能否适应科莱拉的生活方式，而语言既是条件，也是象征。在小说中，卡钱既通过叙述声音，也就是形式，突出这一点，又通过把俚语问题作为主要主题，也就是内容，来加以突出。
en: Aktunç stresses that “the greatest slang treasure of a language is born and bred in the metropolis of that language” (2015, 383). In the novel, the emphasis on Kolerite slang as an urban language implies the urbanity of Kolerites, which is an alternative urbanity. Kolerites rescue the authority to decide who is an urbanite and who is not from the hands of the elite hegemony: being an urbanite is an issue of being able to adapt to the way of life in Kolera, and language is both a condition and a symbol of it. In the novel, Kaçan accents this with the narrative voice (i.e., with form), as well as by problematising the issue of slang as a major theme (i.e., with content).

zh: 如上面的例子所示，小说中的农民无论男女都粗鲁、无知，与科莱拉人差别极大。科莱拉女性与农民女性之间的差别尤其鲜明。
en: As illustrated in the examples above, in the novel both peasant men and women are rude, ignorant and highly different from Kolerites. The differences between the Kolerite women and the peasant women are even more striking.

zh: 科莱拉的女性

对科莱拉的男人而言，适应城市文化比女性更容易，因为后者与街头、与家庭以外生活的联系极其有限。阿里与伊米内的差别，恰好表现了科莱拉城市化的这一性别维度。为了自由地与住在科莱拉的妓女发生性关系，阿里用城市的危险吓唬妻子，把她留在家中。阿里与儿子格利、雷乔都是科莱拉人，而伊米内虽然没有被归入农民一类，却常常与乡村文化联系在一起。例如，萨多被杀后，伊米内看到格利绝望不已，就为他唱了一首“她在村里学会的逗趣童谣”（32）。这首童谣构成巴赫金意义上的嵌入体裁，突出了口头文化在科莱拉和小说中的影响。下一页，伊米内又用香驱除雷乔身上的邪眼。对这种带有萨满色彩的仪式的细致描写，强调了伊米内源于乡村文化的超自然信仰。另一处，叙述者把她的剪刀称为“她从村里带来的大地毯剪”（20），再次暗示她的乡村背景。
en: For the men in Kolera it is easier to adapt to urban culture than women, whose connection with the streets, with life outside the home, is minimal. The differences between Ali and İmine is a perfect manifestation of this gendered dimension of urbanisation in Kolera. In order to freely have sex with prostitutes living in Kolera, Ali keeps his wife at home by scaring her about the city. While Ali and his sons Gıli and Reco are Kolerites, İmine, although not categorised as a peasant, is frequently associated with rural culture. For instance, after Sado gets killed, seeing Gıli in despair, she sings for him a “funny nursery rhyme which she learned in the village” (32). The nursery rhyme, which serves as an inserted genre in the Bakhtinian sense, accentuates the influence of oral culture in Kolera and in the novel. On the following page, İmine uses incense sticks to rescue Reco from the evil eye. The detailed description of this somehow shamanistic ritual emphasises İmine’s belief in the supernatural, stemming from her rural culture. At another instance the narrator describes her scissors as “the big carpet scissors she brought from the village” (20), once again implying her rural background.

zh: 阿里与伊米内迁入一个富裕街区后，伊米内开始化妆，言谈也像城市中产阶级女性。卡钱并没有把伊米内的“城市化”描绘为依次经历各阶段的进步过程。相反，这种变化更像一个滑稽因素，因为伊米内学会城市人的举止时，也失去了理智。在这个意义上，卡钱没有在书中就生活在科莱拉、过着幽闭生活的迁入女性如何获得城市身份提出论证。
en: After Ali and İmine move to a rich neighbourhood, İmine starts wearing makeup and speaking like urban middle-class women. Kaçan does not illustrate İmine’s ‘urbanisation’ as a progression with successive stages. On the contrary, this change appears rather as a comic element, since at the stage when İmine adopts urban manners she also loses her sanity. In this sense, in the book Kaçan does not offer an argument regarding how migrant women living claustrophobic lives in Kolera can adopt an urban identity.

zh: 至于科莱拉那些摆脱束缚、没有被“囚禁”在家中的女性，则完全是另一番景象。下面这段早在小说第二页就把这一点作为重要主题提出，值得讨论：
en: When it comes to the liberated women of Kolera who are not ‘captive’ at home, it is a completely different story. The excerpt below, introducing this as an important theme already on the second page of the novel, is worthy of discussion:

zh: 太阳正从云缝里钻出来，科莱拉的狂欢女客们已在那些仿佛肩膀一撞就会倒塌的房屋前，像狮子一样，和修车工、木匠、车工交谈起来。与此同时，她们开始为那些一边焊接一边双手发抖的手艺人制作过滤嘴，好让他们更尽兴地抽大麻烟。一些农妇像囚犯一样从窗口望着，因为她们被丈夫讲述的街区恐怖故事吓住了。（10）
en: As the sun was wriggling through the clouds, the reveller women of Kolera started conversing like lions with car repairers, carpenters and turners in front of their houses, which looked like they would fall down with a shoulder charge. Meanwhile, they started preparing filters for the craftsmen, whose hands were shaking as they were welding, to smoke their joints more grandly. Some peasant women were watching from the window like prisoners, since they were frightened by the scary stories about the neighbourhood told by their husbands. (10)

zh: “狂欢女客”指参与夜生活的女人。她们可能做过或正在做妓女、陪酒女、酒吧歌手或舞者，也可能与毒贩有过或仍有联系。

这些并不确定。可以确定的是，她们喜欢酒精和大麻。后来，我们又听到“受敬重的狂欢大姐”（94）这一说法。叙述者并没有把所有狂欢女客都称为“受敬重的狂欢大姐”；这是一个声望更高的类别。狂欢女客坚强、受人尊重，实际上与受敬重的男人平等。小说后面出现连环杀手时，只有这些狂欢女客与比蒂里姆敢于出现在街上（94）。在上面这段中，叙述者用“像狮子一样”这一赞许的比喻，描写她们与男人交谈的方式。该段还让人注意到，她们通过帮助男人卷大麻烟，表现出支持性的行为。引文最后一句揭示了她们与农妇之间巨大的差异。这里有一点需要说明：“农妇”可能包括伊米内这样所有待在家里的女性。换言之，即使丈夫是科莱拉人，妻子也可能属于农妇一类。伊米内与阿里的关系就是这种情况。叙述者没有把伊米内归为农民，却强调她的乡村背景；她的丈夫阿里则显然是个科莱拉男人。之所以如此，是因为科莱拉的男人有种种走上街区街头的方式。如该段暗示，他们可以是修车工、木匠或车工等等。然而，这些男人却让妻子待在家中。因为与男人不同，女性并没有多种走上科莱拉街头的途径。于是，这些女人留在家中，仍然是农民；丈夫们却在街上变成了科莱拉人，获得城市身份。
en: “Reveller women” means women who are involved in nightlife. These women might (have) work(ed) as prostitutes, B-girls, singers or dancers in bars; they might also have (had) connections with drug dealers.

This is not certain. What is certain is that they enjoy alcohol and marijuana. Later, we hear the phrase “respectable senior sister revellers” (94). The narrator does not refer to all reveller women as “respectable senior sister revellers”, this is a more prestigious category. Reveller women are strong and respected women who are practically equal to respected men. When a serial killer appears in the later pages of the novel, these reveller women and

are the only ones who have the courage to be out on the streets (94). In the above passage, the narrator uses the praising simile of “like lions” to describe their way of having a conversation with men. The paragraph also draws attention to their supportive behaviour towards men, since they help them by preparing their joints. The final sentence of the quote elucidates the wide discrepancy between them and peasant women. A point should be clarified here: “peasant women” might include all women who are indoors, like İmine. In other words, women whose husbands are Kolerites may also belong to the peasant women category. The relationship of İmine and Ali is such a case. The narrator does not categorise İmine as a peasant, but puts emphasis on her rural background; while her husband Ali seems to be a Kolerite man. This is so, because for men in Kolera various ways of being out on the streets of the neighbourhood exist. As implied in the paragraph, they can be car repairers, carpenters or turners and so on. These men, however, tell their wives to stay indoors. Because unlike the case with men, multiple ways of being out on the streets of Kolera are not available for women. So these women, staying at home, remain as peasants while their husbands, out on the streets, transform into Kolerites, adopting an urban identity.

zh: 小说进行到一半时，“美洲狮泽赫拉”，一位曾经做过陪酒女、在科莱拉十分受敬重的女性，决定献身于教育“科莱拉无知的女人们”：“她要让她们打破男人世界的残酷规矩”（60）。叙述者解释说，对于美洲狮泽赫拉登门拜访，这些女人的丈夫无从发作。“无知的女人”似乎指具有乡村文化、而丈夫已是科莱拉人的女性。换言之，科莱拉男人的妻子并不是农妇，而是无知的女人。经过美洲狮泽赫拉的教育，这些女人极短时间内就开始像比蒂里姆那样行动，出入地下咖啡馆：“她们成了那些连男人都得再三考虑、心怀畏惧才敢进去的咖啡馆的常客”（60），并且成了出色的赌徒。深夜，她们独自在街上行走，嘲弄那些试图骚扰她们的粗野家伙。如果不愿意，她们就拒绝与丈夫发生性关系。仅凭美洲狮泽赫拉的引导，就让女性发生这样的转变，听起来像基于夸张的幽默因素。因此，与伊米内的故事相似，科莱拉受隔绝女性的转变，再次作为一个处理得相当表面的滑稽因素出现。
en: Halfway through the novel, Puma Zehra, a former B-girl who is a highly respectable woman in Kolera, decides to dedicate herself to educating the “ignorant women of Kolera”: “she would make them break the cruel rules of the men’s world” (60). The narrator explains that these women’s husbands cannot react to Puma Zehra’s visits to their homes. “Ignorant women” seems to define women with a rural culture whose husbands are Kolerites. In other words, Kolerite men’s wives are not peasant women but they are ignorant women. After Puma Zehra educates these women they start acting like

within a very short time and start hanging out in the underground coffeehouses: “they have become regular clientele of the coffeehouses to which even men would enter faint-heartedly after thinking more than twice” (60), and become perfect gamblers. Late at night they walk on their own in the streets, ridicule the rough guys who attempt to disturb them. They refuse to have sex with their husbands if they do not fancy it. Such a transformation of women solely as an outcome of Puma Zehra’s guidance sounds like an element of humour based on exaggeration. Thus, similar to İmine’s story, once again, Kolera’s isolated women’s transformation appears as a superficially addressed comic element.

zh: 总之，科莱拉有相当多坚强、受人尊重、丝毫不落后于男性的女性。她们不是平凡的家庭主妇，而是拥有独特生活方式的人。然而，对于那些被隔绝在家中、以家庭主妇身份度过一生的迁入女性而言，与自己居住的街区、进而与城市建立联系，几乎不可能。与住在普通贫困街区、可以安全出门的女性相比，生活在科莱拉这样紧张不安的地方，使她们的生活更加困难。卡钱突出了科莱拉女性被隔绝在室内的处境，却没有进一步讨论她们适应城市生活的可能性。他没有赋予她们科莱拉人身份，只把她们搁置为无知的女人，没有充分地把她们的处境作为问题提出。
en: To sum up, Kolera has a considerable number of women who are strong and respected, and not a step behind the men. These are not mundane housewives; they have a unique lifestyle. However, when it comes to the migrant women who are isolated in their homes and spend their lives as housewives, connecting with the neighbourhood they live in, and therefore with the city, is almost impossible. Living in an edgy place like Kolera makes life more difficult for them compared with the women who live in ordinary poor neighbourhoods where they can safely go out. Kaçan accentuates the condition of Kolera’s women isolated indoors, but does not elaborate on their possibilities of adapting to an urban life. He does not offer the Kolerite identity to them and puts them away as ignorant women without properly problematising their situation.

zh: 世界主义的科莱拉

A. 厄梅尔·蒂尔凯什把科莱拉描述为“一个位于伊斯坦布尔心脏、却又离它十分遥远的街区”（1999，118）。与蒂尔凯什类似，耶尔德兹·埃杰维特把科莱拉人看作“尽管生活在文化大都市，却无法与那种文化建立联系的人”（1991，13）。虽然她赞扬这部小说，埃杰维特仍无法避免再生产一种精英主义且带有偏见的话语，蒂尔凯什的评论中也存在这种话语。首先，什么是伊斯坦布尔的文化？埃杰维特所说的“文化大都市”究竟指什么，并不清楚。如果她指的是精英学校、排他的社交圈，那么的确，科莱拉人无法与那种文化建立联系。又或者，如果她指参与城市中的艺术活动，如歌剧、戏剧或艺术展览，那么也的确如此。然而，与文化建立联系，并不是如此简单而确定的问题。比如，从雷蒙德·威廉斯把文化定义为“一种整体的生活方式”（2001，11）的角度来看，科莱拉人与他们生活的大都市文化有着紧密联系，甚至可能比许多就读名校、关注艺术的人联系得更深，下文将加以讨论。
en: A. Ömer Türkeş describes Kolera as “a neighbourhood at the heart of Istanbul, yet very far away from it” (1999, 118). In line with Türkeş, Yıldız Ecevit views Kolerites as “people who, despite living in a metropolis of culture, cannot establish a connection with that culture” (1991, 13). Although she praises the novel, Ecevit cannot avoid reproducing an elitist and prejudiced discourse, which is also present in Türkeş’s remark. To begin with, what is the culture of Istanbul? It is not clear what Ecevit means by “a metropolis of culture”. If she means elite schools, exclusive social circles, then, true, the people of Kolera cannot connect with that culture. Or, if she means being a part of the arts in the city such as opera, theatre or art exhibitions, in that case it is also true. However, connecting with culture is not such a simple and definite issue. In terms of Raymond Williams’s definition of culture as “a whole way of life” (2001, 11), for instance, Kolerites are closely connected with the culture of the metropolis in which they live, maybe more than many of those who go to the city’s prestigious schools and follow the arts, as discussed below.

zh: 具有不同宗教与族群背景的人在科莱拉共同生活。如前所述，科莱拉俚语包含街区内各种语言的词汇。迈克尔·赫斯解释，小说把罗姆人称为“şopar”，这是罗姆语中的“男孩”（1998，57）。他又补充说：“除罗姆人之外，还有说罗姆语的希腊人（Rum）、叙利亚人（Süryani）、亚美尼亚人（Ermeni）和犹太人（Yahudi）。与罗姆人不同，他们都明确以自己的族群名称被识别。犹太人只被顺带提过一次，而其余三个群体在全书中都发挥着重要作用”（58）。
en: In Kolera people from various religious and ethnic backgrounds live together. As mentioned above, Kolerite slang includes words from different languages used in the neighbourhood. Michael Hess explains that Romani people are called “

” in the novel, which is the Romani word for “boy” (1998, 57). He adds that “besides the Roma there are Romani speaking Greeks (Rum), Syrians (Süryani), Armenians (Ermeni) and Jews (Yahudi). In contrast to the Romany, they are identified explicitly by their ethnic names. While Jews occur once and in passing, the three other groups mentioned play an important role throughout the whole book” (58).

zh: 小说开头，希腊少数群体的成员与科莱拉的索夫塔之间发生了冲突。格利坐在店前的椅子上，目睹索夫塔袭击正要去教堂的希腊人。对事件的描写突出了叙述者对希腊人的同情，以及对索夫塔的厌恶。“富人和那帮凡科莱拉发生什么都要插上一手的索夫塔，非得伤害那些衣着一尘不染、原本安然去教堂的希腊人，才觉得痛快”（15）。
en: At the beginning of the novel, a conflict between the members of the Greek minority and the
of Kolera takes place. Sitting on a chair in front of the shop, Gıli witnesses the
’ attack on the Greek community going to their church. The description of the event emphasises the narrator’s sympathy for the Greeks and his hatred for the

. “The rich and the softa crew who intervened in anything happening in Kolera didn’t feel good until they were hurting the Greeks, who were going to their church in their spotless outfit unhindered” (15).

zh: 赫尔屈尔·米拉斯让人注意到作品在少数群体问题上的现实主义，并将作者梅廷·卡钱与土耳其文学中杰出的短篇小说家萨伊特·法伊克相比较，以此赞美他；后者以笔下令人难忘的非穆斯林人物著称：“他像萨伊特·法伊克一样，准确地理解希腊人。而且接纳他们：蒂娜、木匠米米、通达人情的埃莱妮”（电子邮件交流，2016年9月21日）。小说特别强调，少数群体与来自安纳托利亚的迁入者在科莱拉共同生活。这一强调反驳了那种几乎暗示正是乡村迁入者把少数群体赶出伊斯坦布尔的怀旧话语。格利童年的一段记忆，鲜明地表现了作为科莱拉生活基本要素的世界主义遗产：“萨利赫小时候，走路还只是慢慢学会，就爬上钟楼，把光着的双脚垂在塔外，凝望着天空”（16）。科莱拉是伊斯坦布尔的世界主义仍然活着的地方。
en: Herkül Millas draws attention to the realism in the work regarding minorities and praises the author Metin Kaçan by comparing him to Sait Faik, the pre-eminent short-story writer of Turkish literature, famous for the unforgettable non-Muslim characters in his works: “He, like Sait Faik, perceives Greeks accurately. And accepts them: Tina, carpenter Mimi, worldly Eleni” (email comm., 21 September 2016). In the novel, there is particular emphasis on the fact that minorities and migrants from Anatolia live together in Kolera. This emphasis contests the nostalgic discourse which (almost) suggests it was the rural migrants who pushed the minorities out of Istanbul. A memory from Gıli’s childhood is a good illustration of the cosmopolitan heritage which is a fundamental aspect of life in Kolera: “Salih, in his infancy, when he was slowly mastering walking, climbed up the bell tower, and hanging his bare feet down the tower gazed into space” (16). Kolera is a place where the cosmopolitanism of Istanbul is still alive.

zh: 卡钱通过让少数群体变得可见，强调科莱拉人拥有自己的文化；它融合了街区内的所有文化，而且是一种城市文化。科莱拉人与农民、索夫塔之间的对立，是小说的核心问题之一，因为科莱拉人包含街区内除农民和索夫塔以外的所有居民。
卡钱不断提及科莱拉人这一概念，强调街区身份与世界主义的团结。
en: By making minorities visible, Kaçan emphasises that Kolerites have a culture of their own which is an amalgamation of all the cultures of the neighbourhood, and this is an urban culture. The opposition between Kolerites on the one hand, and the peasants and the
on the other is one of the central issues of the novel as Kolerites include all the inhabitants of the neighbourhood except the peasants and the
With endless references to the concept of Kolerites, Kaçan lays emphasis on neighbourhood identity and cosmopolitan solidarity.

zh: 接近小说结尾时，在一场未具名战争的影响下，街区发生了小规模的族群迫害。
在这一事件中，索夫塔与农民袭击科维诺人，
将他们赶出科莱拉。描写这一事件的段落值得长引：
en: Towards the end of the novel, there is a small-scale pogrom in the neighbourhood under the influence of a war that is not named.
In this event, the
and the peasants attack the
and push them out of Kolera. The passage depicting the event is worth quoting at length:

zh: 那些骗子天刚亮就开始实施前一晚准备好的诡计，恶狠狠地盯着科维诺人的脸，撒下苦难的种子。直到昨天还与科维诺人称兄道弟的商贩，为了财物，变成了变色龙。
en: Shicers, who start in the first light of the morning to realise the trick plans they prepared the night before, staring dirtily at the faces of
, scattered seeds of torment. Tradesmen who were fraternal with
until yesterday turned into chameleons for the sake of goods and chattels.

zh: 科维诺人提着小小的行李箱，在比蒂里姆的保护下离开科莱拉，在通往未来的黑暗道路上磨破鞋子。离去时，他们回望自己付出一生的街区，看到衣服脱离晾绳、灰泥从楼上剥落、挂着风干的鱼也飞上了天空！
en: , leaving Kolera with their small suitcases under protection of the bitirims, wore their shoes out on the dark roads of the future. When they looked, as they were going, at the neighbourhood to which they had given their lives, they saw clothes freed from their ropes, plaster fallen down from the building and fishes hung out to be dried flying in the air!

zh: 那些以区区小钱攫取科维诺人房产与财物的人，把自己的荣誉与调解人的处世准则全都抛到了九霄云外。而平时连两个词都串不起来的农民，却觉得科维诺人受到的不公对待是对的，用他们积攒许久的话赞同科莱拉的索夫塔：［带着乡村口音］“你说啥呀，老兄，现在已经太晚啦！事情就是这样嘛。”（142）
en: Those who went through the buildings and goods of
s for mere chickenfeed threw their honour and fixer mentality up in the air. And peasants who are normally unable to string two words together, finding the injustice done to the
s right, approved of the softas of Kolera using words they had long saved: [in a rural accent] “What are you saying man, it is too late now! That’s just the way it is.” (142)

zh: 拥有非穆斯林居民的科莱拉，承载着伊斯坦布尔失去少数群体之前的身份。它是一座融合不同宗教与族群背景者的熔炉：非穆斯林、罗姆人，以及来自安纳托利亚各地的迁入者。小说开头，叙述者把格利的父亲阿里称为“Yıkıkköprülü Berber Ali”，即“来自耶克克桥的理发师阿里”（10），并解释说：“他再也离不开这个服兵役时见过的街区；后来，他离开了自己的同乡，与妻子一起在科莱拉定居”（14）。如前所述，伊斯坦布尔的迁入者通常住在同乡聚居的街区。阿里为科莱拉着迷，拒绝了城中同乡共同体的舒适地带。搬到科莱拉，是他城市化过程中的重要飞跃。像阿里一样能够适应科莱拉的街区居民，全都是科莱拉人。科莱拉人就是城市居民：一个人不可能既是科莱拉人，又是农民或索夫塔。
en: Kolera, with its non-Muslim residents, carries the identity of Istanbul before it lost its minorities. It is a melting pot of people from different religious and ethnic backgrounds: non-Muslims, the Romani people and migrants from various parts of Anatolia. At the beginning of the novel the narrator describes Ali, Gıli’s father, as “Yıkıkköprülü Berber Ali” (Ali the Barber from Yıkıkköprü) (10) and explains that “he could never be separated from this neighbourhood which he had seen during his military service; and then moved away from his fellow townspeople and settled in Kolera with his wife” (14). As mentioned earlier, migrants in Istanbul usually dwell in neighbourhoods where people from their hometown live. Under the spell of Kolera, Ali rejects the comfort zone of his hometown community in the city. Moving to Kolera is an important leap forward in his urbanisation. Inhabitants of the neighbourhood like Ali who are able to adapt to Kolera are all Kolerites. A Kolerite is an urbanite: one cannot be a Kolerite and a peasant, or a

zh: 赫斯认为，“小说提到波兰诗人亚当·密茨凯维奇，足以使科莱拉就是多拉普代雷街区这一判断不容置疑”（1998，56）。

科莱拉似乎是多拉普代雷的虚构版本，同时也从毗邻的几个街区汲取灵感。卡钱对此解释说：“我在小说中称为科莱拉的地方，实际上包含托普哈内、卡瑟姆帕夏、多拉普代雷、耶尼谢希尔、库尔图卢什、巴拉特和法提赫等街区”（Kaçan 1991，14）。作者本人来自多拉普代雷，他创造科莱拉，映照这些街区的世界主义特征。这样一来，他把城市的世界主义形象从精英主义者对旧伊斯坦布尔的怀念中夺回，并表明：世界主义的肌理，也可以存在于被当作贫困街区而看低、甚至被污名化为衰败之地的区域中。
en: Hess argues that “the identification of Kolera with the Dolapdere quarter is placed beyond any doubt by the mention made in the novel of the Polish poet Adam Mickiewicz” (1998, 56).

While Kolera seems like the fictional version of Dolapdere, it is inspired by several neighbourhoods adjacent to it as well. Kaçan clarifies this as follows: “the place I refer to as Kolera in the novel actually includes the neighbourhoods such as Tophane, Kasımpaşa, Dolapdere, Yenişehir, Kurtuluş, Balat and Fatih” (Kaçan 1991, 14). The author himself, a man from Dolapdere, created Kolera as a reflection of these neighbourhoods’ cosmopolitan character. Doing that, he rescues the cosmopolitan image of the city from the old Istanbul nostalgia of elitists, and demonstrates that the cosmopolitan fabric can be present in an area looked down on as a poor neighbourhood, or even stigmatised as deteriorated.

zh: 科莱拉远远不只是一个供人居住的地方。要理解这一点，最好借助亨利·列斐伏尔的“栖居”概念；他将其解释为“参与社会生活，参与一个共同体、村庄或城市。城市生活在其他品质之外，还具有这一属性。它赋予栖居的权利，使城镇居民—公民能够栖居”（1996，76）。列斐伏尔解释说，城市“连同其街道与广场、建筑与纪念物”，首先应当服务于“节庆（la Fête，一种非生产性的消费庆典，耗费大量金钱和物品财富，除了欢愉与声望，并无其他益处）”（66）。格利居住的贫困街区，被精英视为与城市脱节；卡钱却动人地描绘了他感受到的这种欢愉。他对历史建筑的痴迷就是绝佳例子：“他是个建筑迷。他的营生，就是凝望那些带凸窗、带装饰的楼房，凝望石砌建筑镶饰的铁门，做白日梦”（35）。
en: Kolera is much more than a place where people simply dwell. This can best be perceived through Henri Lefebvre’s concept “to inhabit”, which he explains as “to take part in a social life, a community, village or city. Urban life had, amongst other qualities, this attribute. It gave the right to inhabit, it allowed townsmen-citizens to inhabit” (1996, 76). Lefebvre explains that the city, “with its streets and squares, edifices and monuments”, should primarily be used for “

(a celebration which consumes unproductively, without other advantage but pleasure and prestige and enormous riches in money and objects)” (66). Kaçan poignantly illustrates this pleasure as felt by Gıli who lives in one of the poor neighbourhoods regarded by the elite as disconnected from the city. His obsession with historical buildings is a perfect example: “He was a building freak. Daydreaming while gazing at buildings with oriel windows and ornaments and inlaid iron doors of stone buildings was his occupation” (35).

zh: 叙述者在下面这段话中的愤怒与失望，同样与欣赏城市作为作品有关：“大选临近时，执政党为了赢取选票，装模作样地给街道铺上沥青，蒙蔽选民的眼睛。科莱拉街那些美好的老鹅卵石，就这样被可怕的沥青吞掉了”（50）。他对科莱拉露天电影院变成停车场的愤慨，表明他依恋的是作为作品的城市：“索夫塔与统治地下世界的头目勾结，又与基金会讨价还价，把电影院占着的地租了九十九年，在那些美好的地方停放有钱皮条客的车”（63）。
拥有这处场地的慈善基金会，本应服务公共利益，却将其用于牟利；居民曾经把露天电影院当作接触文化、享受娱乐的地方，这种做法侵害了他们的城市权利。
en: The narrator’s anger and disappointment in the following statement is similarly related to the appreciation of the city as

: “When the general elections approached, the ruling party, in order to win votes, phonily asphalted the streets and threw dust in the voters’ eyes. And good old cobblestones of Kolera Street were swallowed up in the horrible asphalt” (50). The resentment about the transformation of Kolera’s outdoor cinema into a car park is an indication of his attachment to the city as

: “softas collaborating with the chief who rules the underground world, and making a bargain with the foundations, rented the site occupied by the cinema for ninety-nine years, and used it for the rich pimps’ cars in those beautiful places” (63).

The charitable foundation in possession of this place uses it for profit, although it is intended for public good, infringing on the right to the city of the residents who once enjoyed this outdoor cinema as a locus of access to culture and entertainment.

zh: 在叙述者的话语中，城市空间被分为三部分：科莱拉所属的贫困街区、富裕街区，以及城市。叙述者把科莱拉描述为贫困街区（kenar mahalle）。这个词因用法不同可能带有贬义，但在小说中没有；相反，它有积极意味。例如，在下面的描写中，在贫困街区长大，暗示着经由艰难生活获得成熟的可能：“蒂娜，她是那些靠三颗橄榄和四分之一个面包长大的贫困街区女孩中，最热情似火的一个”（124）。贫困街区包含一种独特的生活方式；在叙述者的描写中，有些事件是“典型的贫困街区事件”（123）。叙述者强调科莱拉人丰富的生活知识，把他们视为有智慧的人，而把富裕地区的居民看作浅薄之辈。在这一比较中，正规学校教育毫无意义，重要的是街头学校。在贫困街区获得的街头知识无价，因为别处学不到。因此，叙述者形容把汽车开到哈米特修理铺的顾客，是在“免费获取边缘地区的生活知识”（56）。科莱拉人对这些外来者持负面看法。叙述者下面这句描写就是好例子：“那些来科莱拉买毒品的粗鄙家伙中的一个”（108）。
en: In the narrator’s discourse, the city space is divided into: poor neighbourhoods, one of which is Kolera; rich neighbourhoods; and the city. The narrator describes Kolera as a poor neighbourhood (

). This can be a derogatory term depending on the usage; in the novel, it is not; on the contrary, it has a positive connotation. In the following depiction, for instance, growing up in a poor neighbourhood implies a potential maturity through hardship: “Tina, she was the most hot-blooded of the poor neighbourhood girls who had grown up with three olives and a quarter loaf of bread” (124). A poor neighbourhood comprises a unique way of life; in the narrator’s description, some events are “typical poor neighbourhood incident[s]” (123). The narrator puts emphasis on Kolerites’ extensive knowledge of life and regards them as being wise, while he perceives the residents of the wealthy areas as superficial people. In this comparison, standard school education does not mean anything, it is the school of the streets that counts. The knowledge of the streets gained in the poor neighbourhood is priceless as it cannot be acquired anywhere else. Therefore, the narrator describes the customers bringing their cars to Hamit’s repair shop as “getting free knowledge about life on the periphery” (56). Kolerites perceive these outsiders negatively. The following description of the narrator is a good example: “one of those boors who have come to Kolera to buy drugs” (108).

zh: 关于富裕街区的信息很简单：只要钱够，谁都可以搬进去并融入其中。阿里凭贩毒挣来的钱，与伊米内做到了这一点；伊米内也立刻变成了中产阶级女性。这一细节表明，小说传达的信息不仅针对富裕街区，也针对整个上层阶级生活方式：教育与出身没有任何意义，任何有足够钱的人都能成为上层阶级的一员。然而，在贫困街区，人需要街头知识与勇气。换言之，在《重罗曼》中，卡钱欣赏科莱拉人的文化资本与社会资本，而这些只能在科莱拉的街头获得；他却淡化了上层阶级的文化资本与社会资本，似乎认为他们除了钱一无所有。因此，他在小说中倾向于把精英、暴发户和拥有黑钱的人等同起来。
en: The message about rich neighbourhoods is simple: with adequate finances anyone can move and integrate into a rich neighbourhood. With the money Ali earns by dealing drugs he and İmine do that, and İmine instantly transforms into a middle-class woman. This detail is an indicator of the novel’s message not only on rich neighbourhoods but also on the entire upper-class way of life: education and background do not have any significance; anyone with sufficient finances can become a member of the upper class. However, in the poor neighbourhood one needs knowledge of the streets and courage. In other words, in

Kaçan appreciates the cultural and social capital of Kolerites, which can only be gained on the streets of Kolera, while he understates the cultural and social capital of the upper classes, whom he seems to perceive as possessing nothing but money. Consequently, he tends to equate the elite, the nouveau riche and people with dirty money with each other in his novel.

zh: 书中，贫困街区与富裕街区以外的地方被称为“城市”，意指市中心。科莱拉人与市中心相连，科莱拉与城市之间并不存在二元对立，下文将进一步讨论。二元对立存在于科莱拉这个贫困街区与富裕街区之间，如以下例子所示。科莱拉的第一台电视机，是费特希从富裕街区偷来的。叙述者形容那是费特希“从一个富人街区顺来的”（58）。连环杀手塔内尔被杀后，叙述者说：“要是塔内尔掷出了两个六点，一切都会不同。也许他现在正住在某个富裕街区，过着傻瓜的日子”（122）。另一处，他又评论说：“格利会到伊米内居住的那些富裕街区，去取人性命”（135）。
en: In the book, places other than poor neighbourhoods and rich neighbourhoods are described as the city, implying the city centre. Kolerites are connected with the city centre, there is no dichotomy between Kolera and the city, as discussed below. The dichotomy is between Kolera the poor neighbourhood and the rich neighbourhoods, as depicted in the following examples. The first television in Kolera is the one which Fethi steals from a rich neighbourhood. The narrator describes it as the one Fethi “ripped off from one of the rich neighbourhoods” (58). After the serial murderer Taner is killed, the narrator says: “If Taner’s dice throw was a double six everything would have been different. Maybe he would be living the life of a dummy in one of the rich neighbourhoods” (122). At another moment, he makes the following comment: “Gıli would stop by the rich neighbourhoods where Imine lives to claim lives” (135).

zh: 小说一开始，读者就能注意到科莱拉与市中心的联系。在第一章中，官员来到科莱拉，查抓未登记的工人，老板们便叫学徒当天躲起来；于是，奥尔罕与朋友们去看电影：“狐狸奥尔罕和他的工友们，穿着油腻的衣服，双手布满老茧，对人生却只懂个皮毛，朝城市心脏地带的电影院走去”（23）。市中心电影院集中的地方是贝伊奥卢；然而，叙述者宁愿称它为“城市的心脏”，而不直呼其名。同样，叙述者说“索夫塔为了庆祝赢得比赛，去了拱廊，坐下来喝酒”（66）；这个我们未能得知名字的拱廊，极有可能就是花拱廊（Çiçek Pasajı）。
en: The reader notices the connection between Kolera and the city centre at the very beginning of the novel. In the first chapter, when the officials come to Kolera to catch unregistered workers, the bosses tell their apprentices to disappear for the day, so Orhan and his friends go to the movies: “Fox Orhan, together with his workfellows in oily clothes, with calloused hands, but only rudimentary knowledge of life, made his way to the cinemas in the heart of the city” (23). The area in the city centre with movie theatres is Beyoğlu; however, the narrator prefers to call it “the heart of the city” rather than by its name. Similarly, when the narrator explains that “softas, to celebrate winning the match, went to the arcade and sat down for drinks” (66), it is most likely that this arcade, whose name we do not learn, is Çiçek Pasajı.

zh: 小说几乎完全发生在科莱拉；人物前往贝伊奥卢时，叙述者就把那里称为“城市”，尽管实际上从科莱拉步行即可到达。读者第一次看到格利身处科莱拉之外，是在他刚成为比蒂里姆的时候；他和朋友们从头目的赌窟敲诈到钱后，“格利与朋友们带着从头目那里榨来的额外现钞，散进了城市的肚腹”（85）。书的第三部分用两页充满趣味的篇幅，讲述格利与朋友们的这段历险。他们先走进一家酒吧，几个喜欢年轻男孩的年长男同性恋者请他们喝啤酒。格利与朋友们以殴打回应这些男人的性挑逗，还打碎了杯盘。叙述者总结他们的历险：“四个伙伴正谈论着，他们怎样在城市香气扑鼻的街头，避免被人操了”（86）。随后他们去妓院：“他们吸着香水味，走进了城市中心的窑子”（86）。格利在这里有了人生第一次性经历，并偷走了妓女的漂亮拖鞋；小说前面，他母亲想买漂亮拖鞋，却买不起。叙述继续道：“格利和朋友们走到窑子通往城市的大门时，像狗一样大笑，笑得肚肠都疼了”（87）。这段以他们返回科莱拉告终：“四个伙伴在街上胡闹，直到狗群占据城市，才嚷叫着走下坡，回到科莱拉”（87）。格利把拖鞋扔上父母家的阳台，眼中噙着几滴泪，走向赌窟过夜。在这段中，格利与朋友们去找妓院的地方，显然是卡拉柯伊的一条街，城中所有妓院都在那里；然而，地名再次没有揭晓，叙述者只是把那里称为“城市”。
en: The novel is almost entirely set in Kolera, and when the characters go to Beyoğlu, the narrator refers to this place as the city, although in fact it is within walking distance of Kolera. The first time the reader witnesses Gıli outside of Kolera is in his early days as a

, after he and his friends extort money in the chief’s gambling den: “Gıli and his friends dispersed to the stomach of the city with the bonus cash they screwed the chief out of” (85). We read this adventure of Gıli and his friends in the third part of the book in a two-page long, highly amusing passage. They first go into a bar where some elderly gay men, who are interested in young boys, buy them beers. Gıli and his friends respond to these men’s sexual advances by attacking them, and they break glasses and plates. The narrator sums up their adventures: “four cronies were talking about how they avoided getting fucked in the perfumed streets of the city” (86). After that they go to a brothel: “breathing in the smell of the perfume they entered the central knocking shop of the city” (86). Here Gıli has sex for the first time in his life, and steals the prostitute’s fancy slippers (earlier in the novel his mother wants to purchase fancy slippers but cannot afford them). The narration continues as follows: “When Gıli arrived at the knocking shop’s door which opens onto the city with his friends, he laughed like a dog until his guts ached” (87). The passage ends when they come back to Kolera: “the four cronies came down screamingly to Kolera after fooling around in the streets until dogs invaded the city” (87). Gıli throws the slippers onto his parents’ balcony, and with a few tears in his eyes walks to the gambling den to spend the night. In this passage, although it is obvious that where Gıli and his friends go to find the brothel is a street in Karaköy, a street where all the brothels of the city are, once again the name of the place is undisclosed, the narrator simply refers to it as the city.

zh: 在这一背景下，另一个值得注意的问题，是雷乔（格利的兄弟）在科莱拉以外的社会交往。通过“他在街区外的朋友”，或“他从外部世界获得的知识”（55）等描述，叙述者强调科莱拉与其外部世界的区别。他这样解释雷乔离开科莱拉的时刻：“他用外套包起书和磁带，出发去见那些在科莱拉之外结交的朋友”（66）。这里，书与音乐磁带表明了他的兴趣。最终，他返回科莱拉，开办漫画图书馆，几乎构成了一个常见母题：一个来自贫困地方的人，最终回乡，通过教育、文化与艺术为乡人作贡献。遗憾的是，雷乔回来时，科莱拉并未热情欢迎他：“他离开任职的报社，奔回来寻找自己遗落在街上的灵魂。雷乔白跑了这一趟；他不知道，离开太久的灵魂，再也回不到身体里”（138）。当他走在科莱拉街头，醉醺醺的诗人高声朗诵诗作，罗姆人说着俏皮话；然而，雷乔再也听不见他们。
en: Another point worthy of notice in this context is Reco’s (Gıli’s brother) socialisation outside of Kolera. With depictions such as “his friends from outside the neighbourhood” or “his knowledge gained from the outside world” (55), the narrator emphasises the distinction between Kolera and the world beyond it. He explains the moment of Reco’s departure from Kolera as follows: “wrapping his books and tapes up in his jacket he set off to meet the friends he made outside Kolera” (66). Here, his books and music tapes indicate his interests. Eventually, he returns to Kolera to open a cartoon library which appears almost as a topos: a person from a poor place eventually comes back home to contribute to his people via education, culture and the arts. Unfortunately, Kolera does not welcome Reco warmly when he returns: “leaving the newspaper he worked for, he ran to find the soul which he had left in the street. Reco ran to Kolera for nothing, he did not know that a soul which is left for a long time will never come back to the body” (138). As he walks in the streets of Kolera, drunken poets are reciting their poems loudly, the Romani people are saying funny words. However, Reco is no longer able to hear them.

zh: 科莱拉人似乎把自己的街区视为自给自足的世界，无须城市其他部分的知识或文化。虽然科莱拉与市中心相连，像“穿着费特希衣服的小伙子们，走上城市的心脏地带，在那些阔佬蠢货面前摆起架子”（48），或“在科莱拉通往城市心脏的沥青路上”（127）这样的描述，却暗示了科莱拉作为自我封闭整体的身份。有一个例子中，叙述者把阿里与伊米内的新家称为“市中心的房子”（134），城市中心与富裕街区在某种程度上重叠了。然而，这里有一个或许值得一提的细节：在上面这类例子中，每当叙述者谈到城市，他都称之为şehir（城市）或şehrin göbeği（城市的心脏）；这是科莱拉人与之有密切联系的市中心，主要是贝伊奥卢——夜生活、文化与艺术的中心，从科莱拉步行即可到达。而当科莱拉之外的城市指的是富裕街区时，叙述者使用kent，而非şehir（127）。这两个词都意为城市，但şehir比kent更口语化。这样的用词或许与前面的论点一致：şehir似乎暗示包含贫困街区在内的城市，kent则似乎带有属于富人和精英的城市空间之意味。
en: Kolerites seem to regard their neighbourhood as a self-sufficient world where they do not need the knowledge or the culture of the rest of the city. Although Kolera is connected with the city centre, descriptions such as “youngsters who put on Fethi’s clothes went up to the heart of the city and put on airs around the loaded dickheads” (48) or “in Kolera’s asphalt road extending to the heart of the city” (127) imply Kolera’s identity as a self-enclosed unity. In one example, the centre of the city and its rich neighbourhoods somewhat overlap when the narrator describes Ali and İmine’s new house as “the house at the centre of the city” (134). However, there is a fine detail here that might be worthy of mention: in all instances where the narrator talks about the city, like the examples above, he calls it
(city) or

(heart of the city): this is the city centre which the Kolerites have a close connection with, mainly Beyoğlu, the heart of the nightlife and culture and arts which is within walking distance of Kolera. In the instance where the city outside of Kolera means rich neighbourhoods, the narrator uses the word
rather than
(127). Both words mean city; however,
is a more colloquial word than
. Such a word choice might be in line with the argument above:
seems to be suggesting the city with its poor neighbourhoods as well, while
seems to have the connotation of the urban space belonging to the rich and the elite.

zh: 简言之，科莱拉自成一个世界；但它是一个伊斯坦布尔的世界，与市中心紧密相连，尤其与贝伊奥卢——夜生活以及文化艺术的中心——紧密相连。科莱拉的大门为想出去的人敞开，却不向想进来的人开放。外人可以来科莱拉修车或买毒品，却无法成为科莱拉共同体的一员。
en: In brief, Kolera is a world unto itself, but it is an Istanbulite world that is closely connected with the city centre, particularly with Beyoğlu, the heart of the nightlife as well as culture and arts. Kolera’s gates are open to those who want to go out but not for those who want to come in. Outsiders might come to Kolera to have their car fixed or to buy drugs, but they cannot be a member of the Kolera community.

zh: 卡钱成功描绘出科莱拉独特的身份，对于他成功挑战“衰败街区”话语至关重要。这种话语使破败、贫困的街区容易遭到服务于资本家利益的严酷城市改造项目的侵袭。话语内含的犯罪问题，导致多拉普代雷、塔尔拉巴舍、苏卢库莱等街区受到污名化。政治人物与官员把这些地方描述为犯罪中心，为在那里推行城市改造项目制造借口。在主流媒体的支持下，这导致人们普遍对这些地方抱有偏见。在《重罗曼》中，卡钱以多拉普代雷及其邻近街区为基础，真实地创造出科莱拉这个包括罪犯在内的各种人共同生活的地方，借此反驳这种污名化。
en: Kaçan’s success in illustrating Kolera’s unique identity is crucial to his achievement of challenging the deteriorated neighbourhood discourse. This discourse renders run-down, poor neighbourhoods prone to harsh urban transformation projects serving the interests of capitalists. The issue of crime inherent in this discourse leads to the stigmatisation of neighbourhoods such as Dolapdere, Tarlabaşı, and Sulukule. Politicians and officials present these places as hubs of crime in order to create an excuse to launch urban transformation projects in them. With the support of the mainstream media, this leads to a widespread prejudice against these places. In
, Kaçan contests this stigmatisation by realistically creating Kolera, based on Dolapdere and adjacent neighbourhoods, where different types of people, including criminals, live together.

zh: 下面这段描写街区寻常早晨的文字，在这一点上值得长引：
en: The following passage depicting an ordinary morning in the neighbourhood is worth quoting at length in this respect:

zh: 黑夜、大海的呼啸、马的嘶鸣、吗啡瘾君子发作时用剃刀割伤自己所发出的尖叫，渐渐变成了早晨。
en: Night, howls of the sea, whinnies of horses, screams of morphine addicts in crises slashing themselves with razors gradually became morning.

zh: 太阳朝地平线上的屋顶揉着惺忪的睡脸，在酒吧里耗尽力气的陪酒女，接二连三地回到科莱拉。造船厂的大门尖厉地开启，像鳄鱼张开巨口，吞下了从金属街道出发的工人。金属街道上那些瘦小、黝黑、干瘪的孩子，怒气冲冲地推起工作坊的卷帘门，仿佛约好同时动手。（22—23）
en: While the sun was rubbing its sleepy face towards roofs on the horizon, B-girls worn out in bars hit Kolera one after the other. The giant door of the shipyard opening stridently, like a crocodile’s mouth, caught the workers who set off from the metal streets. Meagre, dark and dry children in the metal streets pushed up the shutters of the workshops they work at angrily as if they have all agreed to do so simultaneously. (22–23)

zh: 显然，这个地方不是犯罪中心。虽然有些被社会排斥的人，如吗啡成瘾者或陪酒女，住在这里，但这段表明，码头工人、店主、学徒等等也在这里生活和／或工作。叙述者把他们全都作为科莱拉人来呈现，对任何人都不抱偏见，不加等级区分。他把科莱拉街区描绘为一个容纳各行各业之人、无人被排除的地方。科莱拉是对受到严重污名化的多拉普代雷及毗邻街区的虚构描写；这样的呈现方式，回应了那种为使这些街区全面绅士化、为严酷城市改造项目辩护而污名化它们的话语。
en: Obviously this place is not a hub of crime. Although some outcasts such as morphine addicts or B-girls live here, the passage demonstrates that workers on the docks, shopkeepers, apprentices and so forth live and/or work here. The narrator presents them all as the people of Kolera without any prejudice against any of them, free from hierarchy. He illustrates the neighbourhood of Kolera as a place which enfolds people from different walks of life, none of them excluded. This way of presenting Kolera as the fictional depiction of heavily stigmatised Dolapdere and the adjacent neighbourhoods is a response to the discourse that stigmatises them in order to justify harsh urban transformation projects for full-scale gentrification of these neighbourhoods.

zh: 《重罗曼》写于这样一项暴力城市改造计划之前二十年；该项目于2010年在多拉普代雷—塔尔拉巴舍地区启动，得到“衰败街区”话语的支持。小说用广泛的人物谱系，以科莱拉之名生动描绘这一区域，是对所谓衰败街区污名化的一声抗议。科莱拉是一个色彩斑斓的舞台，善与恶并存。在小说中，卡钱并不把恶与涉足轻微犯罪或毒品的人联系起来。黑帮、为私利滥用权力的腐败官员和警察，以及与他们勾结的人，才是恶的化身。在科莱拉，也在小说中，判断善恶的标准不是犯罪，而是荣誉准则。
en: was written twenty years before one such violent urban transformation project, which was launched in the Dolapdere-Tarlabaşı area in 2010, supported by the deteriorated neighbourhood discourse. With a wide array of characters enabling a vivid picture of the area in the guise of Kolera, the novel is a cry against the stigmatisation of so-called deteriorated neighbourhoods. Kolera is an arena of multiple colours where the good and the evil live side by side. Kaçan does not associate the evil with those involved in petty crime or drugs in his novel. The mafia, corrupt officials and the police who abuse their power for their own interests, and those who collaborate with them, are the embodiment of the evil. In Kolera and in the novel, crime is not the criterion of being good or evil, the honour code is.

zh: 与那种只把科莱拉这样的地方污名化为犯罪中心的话语相反，卡钱强调科莱拉共同体的异质性。事实上，对于许多科莱拉人来说，街区内的犯罪与对于城市安静地带的居民而言同样可怕；许多段落描写了“科莱拉的好人不敢走进去的街道”（30），以及“那些没有面孔的人夜里游荡的街道，科莱拉的好人白天都不敢走”（40）。理发师阿里在街区生活的故事，同样是一个说明问题的例子。小说很早就写到，阿里还是个年轻小伙、正在服兵役时，就被科莱拉吸引；结婚后终于搬到这里。他在这里的生活并不轻松：“为了保护自己，不受药丸瘾君子、疯子、吃白食的无赖伤害，同时又能在科莱拉站住脚，他把命攥在手里，拼死搏斗”（14）。看到被头目的手下杀害的人流出的血就在自己店门前时，阿里忍无可忍：“这不是正经人住的地方！”（34）他大喊道。然而，直到妻子失去理智，他才终于采取最后的行动，离开科莱拉。这是一个难以生活下去、却更难割舍的地方。
en: As opposed to the discourse which stigmatises places like Kolera solely as hubs of crime, Kaçan underscores the heterogeneity of the Kolerite community. In fact, for many Kolerites, crime in the neighbourhood is as scary as it would be for inhabitants of the quiet parts of the city, as many passages depict “streets which the good people of Kolera would not dare to go into” (30); “Kolera’s good people would not dare to walk in the daytime in the streets where these faceless men were wandering at night” (40). The story of barber Ali’s life in the neighbourhood is also a telling example of that. As noted very early in the novel, Ali gets drawn to Kolera when he is a young boy on military service, and eventually moves there as a married man. His life there is not painless: “in order to defend himself from pillheads, psychos, freeloading rowdies, and at the same time to be able to get a toehold in Kolera, he was battling with his life in his hands” (14). When in front of his shop he sees the blood of men killed by the chief’s men, Ali comes to the end of his tether: “these are not places where proper people would live” (34) he yells. However, only when his wife loses her sanity can he eventually make the final move to leave Kolera. It is a place that is difficult to live within yet more difficult to live without.

zh: 叙述者清楚地描述了格利对科莱拉的感受：“尽管有这一切，这样的街区还是让人不可能离开”（106）。他的兄弟雷乔离开街区这一事件，暗示了科莱拉令人上瘾、不可或缺的特质：“雷乔走近科莱拉边缘时，百感交集。与这些把欢笑和热烈生活视作生命一部分的街坊分离，让他深深难过”（66）。
en: The narrator lucidly describes Gıli’s feelings about Kolera: “a neighbourhood like this was impossible to leave despite everything” (106). His brother Reco’s departure from the neighbourhood is an event in the novel that implies Kolera’s addictiveness and indispensability: “When Reco approached the edge of Kolera his feelings were mixed. Separating from the people of the neighbourhood who made laughing and living impassionedly a part of their life, touched him badly” (66).

zh: 叙述者不断强调科莱拉及其居民的独特身份。他第一次讲到街区的夜晚时，赌徒来到奥尔索的咖啡馆，其秘密顶楼用作赌场；警察追赶妓女，抽大麻的人则跳舞取乐。小偷让猫跳上地毯，以便偷走地毯；阿里在自家阳台下逮住了他们，叙述者评论说：“对住在街区的人来说，这些事不过是午夜的乐子”（20）。正如下列引文所示，听觉与嗅觉意象是小说的核心特征，在描绘科莱拉这个充满个性、又让人紧张不安的街区时，发挥着重要作用：“在破碎针筒的阴影下长大的科莱拉孩子”（15）；“响着刀声、骰子声和诱人尖叫声的科莱拉街道”（55）；“科莱拉总有的油漆稀释剂、烧焦轮胎和油漆的气味”（43）；“响着杯形鼓声的科莱拉街道”（71）；“科莱拉严酷的日夜生活”（98）；“教堂钟声充满空气，与淡淡的大麻气味和宣礼声混在一起”（13）；“铁匠、废品商和‘皇帝们’有规律的锤击声，像一面上好杯形鼓的声音，散入空中”（23）。
en: The narrator constantly accents the unique identity of Kolera and its people. The first time he tells about a night in the neighbourhood, gamblers arrive at Orso’s coffeehouse, which has a secret top floor for gambling; the police chase prostitutes while marijuana smokers dance and have fun. Thieves make cats jump onto carpets to steal them, Ali catches them under his balcony and the narrator comments: “for those living in the neighbourhood such incidents were nothing but midnight fun” (20). As the following excerpts demonstrate, the use of auditory and olfactory imagery, a central feature of the novel, has an important function in Kolera’s depiction of this characterful and edgy neighbourhood: “Kolera’s children who have grown up in the shade of broken syringes” (15); “Kolera’s streets with the sounds of knives, dice and seductive screams” (55); “the smell of paint thinner, burned tyres, paint that is always in Kolera” (43); “Kolera’s streets with the sound of the darbuka” (71); “Kolera’s tough night and day life” (98); “bell chimes from the church filled the air mixing with a soft odour of marihuana and the sound of the azan” (13); “the regular hammer beats of the smiths, junk dealers and ‘emperors’ dispersed into the air like the sound of a good quality darbuka” (23).

zh: 如第2章所述，理查德·桑内特解释，酒神仪式“最适宜在陌生人之间进行：如果没有人知道你是谁、从哪里来，喝酒、跳舞与性交就会更加狂烈”（1992，238）。然而，在科莱拉，即使人们彼此十分熟悉，酒神仪式依然举行。科莱拉是桑内特的酒神之城的独特版本。与此同时，它也是一个普通的贫困街区，各行各业的人在这里共同生活，努力靠劳动求生。正如赫尔屈尔·米拉斯所言：“人们会以为这是个残酷的地方，可并非如此；若有需要，几乎每个人都会‘高尚地’接纳需要帮助的人”（电子邮件交流，2016年9月21日）。总之，科莱拉所怀抱的，远比“衰败街区”这个贬义概念暗示的要丰富。小说通过强调这一事实来抵抗污名化，大声疾呼穷人有权栖居在市中心自己的街区中。
en: As mentioned in Chapter 2, Richard Sennett explains that Dionysiac rites “could be practiced best among strangers: the drinking, dancing, and fucking is more intense if no one knows who you are or where you come from” (1992, 238). In Kolera, however, Dionysiac rites are carried out even though the people know each other very well. Kolera is a unique version of Sennett’s Dionysiac city. At the same time, it is yet another poor neighbourhood where people from all walks of life live together and try to survive on their labour. As Herkül Millas observes: “one would think it is a cruel place, but it is not; if need be, almost everybody ‘nobly’ embraces the one who needs help” (email comm., 21 September 2016). In short, Kolera carries much more in its bosom than the pejorative concept of deteriorated neighbourhood suggests. The novel, countering stigmatisation by emphasising this fact, is a loud cry for the right of the poor to inhabit their neighbourhoods in the city centre.

zh: 结论

书中有一处，叙述者告诉我们：“不论在科莱拉，还是在世界其他边缘地带，都没有人敢对美洲狮泽赫拉说三道四”（60）。“世界其他边缘地带”是作者富于诗意的表述，承载着诸多含义：贫困街区在小说中表现为一种存在方式，一个自成一体的世界。另一处，叙述者把费特希形容为“科莱拉唯一拥有健康、闪亮牙齿的人”（34），令人心酸地暗示了科莱拉人的贫穷。小说中有大量这样的表达，描写贫困街区科莱拉居民的生活。奥尔罕·凯末尔等作家已经在现代土耳其小说中描绘过这样的生活。《重罗曼》的独特之处在于，叙述者用科莱拉俚语讲述，将自己呈现为贫困街区居民中的一员。
en: At one point in the book, the narrator tells us that “neither in Kolera, nor in other peripheries of the world was there someone who would dare to say a word to Puma Zehra” (60). “Other peripheries of the world”, a poetic phrase of the author, is laden with meanings: a poor neighbourhood appears in the novel as a way of being, a world unto itself. At another moment, the narrator describes Fethi as “the only person in Kolera with healthy and shiny teeth” (34), poignantly implying Kolerites’ poverty. The novel has numerous examples of such articulations depicting the lives of people in the poor neighbourhood of Kolera. Such lives have been depicted in modern Turkish novel by authors such as Orhan Kemal. What makes
unique is the way the narrator presents himself as one of the inhabitants of the poor neighbourhood by narrating in Kolerite slang.

zh: 如上所述，作品拥有如此生动、多彩的人物群像，只有内部人才写得出来。在小说中，卡钱把所有人物都放在科莱拉生活不可或缺的位置上。在最后一次访谈中，他作出这样的评论：“作为一个在多拉普代雷长大的人，我从未评判或羞辱过同性恋者、杀人犯、宗教狂热者或妓女。对我来说，他们都有故事要讲。他们都是最初带着美好故事上路的人。接受他们本来的样子，不评判他们，是多拉普代雷的生活教给我的东西之一。随着时间推移，这些人中的大多数成了我的朋友”（Kaçan 2012，11）。“不曾看低他们中的任何一个”，在这里是重要的表述，突出了卡钱在作品中取得的成就。如上所述，卡钱在整部小说中都强调，已经适应城市生活方式的迁入者与尚未适应者之间存在对照。他“没有看低他们中的任何一个，也没有评判任何一个”，这是真的。不过，小说中科莱拉人与农民、索夫塔之间的对立，如果出现在另一种语境中，可能听起来像一种评判手段。它在《重罗曼》中并不显得是一种评判，因为卡钱把成为城市居民的道路设定为一条向所有人开放的道路：要成为城市居民，不需要父母出生于城市，不需要良好的学校教育，也不需要小资产阶级社交圈；一个人必须欣赏城市的多样性，才能成为城市居民。这是卡钱在字里行间传达的信息。
en: As discussed above, the work boasts such a vivid and colourful variety of characters that it could only be written by an insider. In his novel, Kaçan positions all the characters as indispensable parts of the life in Kolera. In his last interview, he makes the following comment: “As a person who grew up in Dolapdere, I have never ever judged or humiliated either homosexuals, or murderers, or religious bigots, or prostitutes. For me they all had a story to tell. They were all people who set off with beautiful stories at the beginning. Accepting them as they are, not judging them were among those things living in Dolapdere has taught me. Most of these people, in time, became my friends” (Kaçan 2012, 11). “Having not looked down on any of them” is an important description here, underscoring what Kaçan has achieved in his work. As discussed above, throughout his novel Kaçan underlines the contrast between migrants who have adapted to an urban way of life and those who have not. He has “not looked down on any of them, judged any of them”, that is true. However, the opposition in the novel, between Kolerites on the one hand, and the peasants and the softas on the other, could sound like a means of judgement, had it appeared within another context. It does not appear as a judgement in

because Kaçan posits the route to becoming an urbanite as a road open to everybody: one does not need to have parents who were born in the city to be an urbanite, neither a good school education nor a petit bourgeois social circle: one has to appreciate the diversity in the city to be an urbanite; this is the message Kaçan conveys between the lines.

zh: 卡钱以反对精英主义态度的方式，将伊斯坦布尔一个贫困街区描绘为差异相遇的地方，而不怀恋旧伊斯坦布尔。在这一点上，作者在同一访谈中的如下话语值得长引：
en: Kaçan depicts a poor neighbourhood of Istanbul as a place where differences meet without the feeling of nostalgia for old Istanbul, in a manner opposed to an elitist attitude. In this respect, the following words of the author from the same interview are worth quoting at length:

zh: 我讲述的人、事、街道，我想要讲述的一切，都以伊斯坦布尔为主角。伊斯坦布尔是我的人物展示才华的舞台。它是一座宏大的舞台，会爱，会恨，会敞开胸怀，同时也会排斥。对我而言，我度过童年的多拉普代雷，在某种意义上就是伊斯坦布尔的缩影。杀人犯、窃贼、迁入家庭、亚美尼亚人、希腊人，所有人都在那里，活生生地存在，无法否认；他们被接纳，同时也被排斥、被他者化。（Kaçan 2012，11）
en: The people, events, streets I tell about, I would like to tell about, all of them have Istanbul in the lead role. Istanbul is a stage where my characters exhibit their talents. A grand stage that loves, hates, opens its bosom and at the same time excludes. Dolapdere, where I spent my childhood, was in a way a microcosm of Istanbul for me. Murderers, thieves, migrant families, Armenians, Greeks all of them were there as large as life, in a way impossible to deny; they were accepted and at the same time excluded, otherised. (Kaçan 2012, 11)

zh: 遗憾的是，这样的多拉普代雷在不久的将来就会只剩回忆。城市改造项目正以令人难以置信的力度与速度使这一区域绅士化，它也随之从视野中消退。《重罗曼》结尾时，阿里家已经没有一个人留在科莱拉：他已离开，妻子作为一个疯女人独自住在富裕街区，雷乔早已离开科莱拉，格利则已经自杀。科莱拉美丽的鹅卵石街道被沥青覆盖，露天电影院变成停车场。书中阴郁的结局，似乎预示了如今正在摧毁城市、尤其是多拉普代雷这类街区的无情城市改造。作者2013年追随自己那位特立独行的主人公的脚步自杀，又给这幅痛苦的图景添上一层暗色。
en: Unfortunately, this Dolapdere will be just a memory in the very near future. It is fading out of sight with the urban transformation project that is gentrifying the area with an incredible intensity and speed. At the end of

no member of Ali’s family is in Kolera: he has left the place, his wife lives on her own as a mad woman in a rich neighbourhood, Reco has long departed from Kolera, and Gıli has committed suicide. The beautiful cobbled streets of Kolera are covered with asphalt, and the outdoor cinema has been transformed into a car park. The grim ending of the book seems to foreshadow the ruthless urban transformation that is now destroying the city, particularly neighbourhoods like Dolapdere. The author’s suicide in 2013, following the footsteps of his idiosyncratic protagonist, makes this painful picture darker.

zh: 正如整个分析所强调的，在《重罗曼》中，卡钱超越城市权利的物质需求层面，从作品，以及对能够栖居其中、欣赏这一作品的市中心的诉求，来处理这一概念。凭借它传达的种种信息、独特的叙述声音以及敏锐的预见，《重罗曼》将永远作为一部关于伊斯坦布尔的重要小说，在现代土耳其文学中占据特殊位置。
en: As stressed throughout the analysis, in
Kaçan surpasses the material needs aspect of the right to the city, and addresses this concept in terms of
and the claim to the city centre where one can inhabit and appreciate this
. With all its messages, with its unique narrative voice and wise foreshadowing,
will always have a special place in modern Turkish literature as a key novel about Istanbul.

zh: 《贝尔吉·克里斯廷：垃圾山的故事》与《重罗曼》：比较分析
en: Berji Kristin: Tales from the Garbage Hills and Heavy Roman(I): A Comparative Analysis

zh: 在形式上，两本书截然不同。《垃圾山的故事》是一部高度实验性的小说，采用片段式结构；《重罗曼》则结构简单，沿直线展开。然而，两者的叙述声音相似。在《垃圾山的故事》中，叙述者使用民间口语中的词汇；在《重罗曼》中，叙述者使用科莱拉俚语。产生的效果，是一个内部人的声音，一个来自他们所描绘的共同体的人的声音。因此，内部人的感觉不仅存在于小说内容中，也存在于形式中。
en: In terms of form, the two books are completely different from each other.
is a highly experimental novel with an episodic structure, while
has a simple and linear structure. However, they are similar in terms of narrative voice. In
, the narrator uses words from folk speech, and in

he uses Kolerite slang. The resulting effect is the sound of an insider, someone from the community they describe. Thus the insider feeling is not only in the content but also in the form of the novels.

zh: 在《垃圾山的故事》中，山民通过某种奇异的炼金术，在自己的魔幻宇宙里，把城市文化的概念变成自身的语言。城市要素以变形的方式进入花山，仿佛置身于幻景。这一虚构地方半乡村、半城市，没有固定形态，既半写实，又半超现实。这个环境的中心，是乡村居民的口头传统。然而，在《重罗曼》中，作为城市现象的俚语才是小说的精髓。在某些时刻，通过主人公母亲的信仰与传统，会出现对乡村口头文化的提及，却没有在书中留下印记。《重罗曼》面朝城市文化，而《垃圾山的故事》主要讲述乡村文化在城中的转变。
en: In

, the Hill folk, by some extraordinary alchemy, turn concepts of urban culture into a language of their own in their magical universe. Urban elements enter Flower Hill in a distorted form, as if in a phantasmagoria. This fictional place is a semi-rural and semi-urban amorphous setting, semi-realistic and semi-surrealistic. At the centre of this setting is the oral tradition of rural people. In

, however, slang, which is an urban phenomenon, is the essence of the novel. At certain moments, through the protagonist’s mother’s beliefs and traditions, references to rural oral culture emerge, but they do not leave their trace in the book. The face of
is turned to urban culture, while
is mainly about rural culture’s transformation in the city.

zh: 花山共同体全是第一代迁入者；而在科莱拉，许多人物，包括主人公格利，都是作为迁入者的子女在伊斯坦布尔出生的。此外，花山的山民刚刚来到城市，而住在科莱拉的第一代迁入者，如格利的父亲阿里，已在伊斯坦布尔生活很久。再者，花山是一个与城市其他部分隔绝的封闭圈子，而科莱拉就在市中心。这一差异深刻影响了两部小说中人物各不相同的城市化过程。
en: The community in Flower Hill are all first-generation migrants, while in Kolera, many of the characters, including the protagonist Gıli, were born in Istanbul as children of migrants. Additionally, while in Flower Hill the Hill folk are migrants who have very recently arrived in the city, the first-generation migrants who live in Kolera, like Gıli’s father Ali, have been in Istanbul for a long while. In addition to this, while Flower Hill is a closed circuit isolated from the rest of the city, Kolera is at the centre of the city. This difference has a profound effect on the characters’ distinct processes of urbanisation in the two novels.

zh: 在《垃圾山的故事》中，泰金把山民描绘得困惑至极，对周围正在发生的生活完全陌生，仿佛来自另一个星球。他们试图理解工会、罢工、男女在纠察线上的交往方式、抗议等等。与此相反，科莱拉人——也就是科莱拉居民中除农民、索夫塔以及生活在室内的家庭主妇以外的人——在城市里感到自在。
en: In

, Tekin portrays the Hill folk in utter perplexity, completely unfamiliar with the life going on around them as if they have arrived from another planet. They try to make sense of a union, a strike, the way men and women socialise on the picket line, protests and so forth. In contrast with that, Kolerites (i.e., the people of Kolera excluding the peasants, the
and the housewives living indoors) feel at ease in the city.

zh: 由于泰金在小说中不聚焦某个特定人物，我们无法观察一个人物在城市身份方面的变化过程；而在《重罗曼》中，作为科莱拉人的城市身份，是格利与雷乔人物塑造的核心。成为科莱拉人就是成为城市人，但卡钱通过格利生活方式呈现的这种城市性带有几分虚无主义，与进步主义者所期待的城市身份不同。格利最后自杀，他的父亲则开始贩毒，以资助自己在富裕街区的新生活。另一方面，谈到雷乔时，卡钱没有把科莱拉人身份与虚无主义及危险躁动的生活方式等同起来；在雷乔身上，科莱拉人的城市性与进步主义视角相当一致。雷乔作为科莱拉人，充分利用生活在市中心的优势，结识来自伊斯坦布尔各地、生活方式不同的人，并参与文化艺术和左翼政治。然而，他在这样做的同时，离开了科莱拉。过了一阵，他回到街区，开办漫画图书馆，为科莱拉年轻人提供另一种存在方式，一条自我实现的通道，而不再只是在赌窟消磨时间。小说关于雷乔的信息是矛盾的。他是保留了科莱拉人身份，并将其扩展到包含新的生活方式与兴趣？还是仅仅以另一种城市身份取代了科莱拉人身份？有一点很清楚：一旦搬走，他就不再像过去那样属于科莱拉。不过，这并不意味着科莱拉因为他离开而惩罚他。此外，小说没有任何话表明雷乔觉得自己高于科莱拉共同体。书末，他是家中唯一没有悲剧结局的人物。我们不知道他此后的故事；它完全可能是积极的，这一事实给作品带来了一点希望。
en: Since Tekin does not focus on a specific character in her novel, it is not possible to observe a character’s dynamics as regards urban identity, while in

the urban identity of being a Kolerite is central to Gıli’s and Reco’s characterisation. Being a Kolerite is being urban, yet the way Kaçan presents this through Gıli’s way of life is somewhat nihilistic, distinct from the urban identity expected by the progressivists. Gıli commits suicide in the end, and his father starts drug dealing to finance a new life in a wealthy neighbourhood. On the other hand, when it comes to Reco, Kaçan does not equate the Kolerite identity with nihilism and an edgy life style; in Reco’s case, urbanity of the Kolerite is quite in line with the progressivist perspective. Reco, as a Kolerite, taking full advantage of living in the city centre, meets people from various parts of Istanbul with different lifestyles, and gets involved with culture and the arts, and leftist politics. However, as he does this, he leaves Kolera. After a while, he comes back to his neighbourhood, and opens a cartoon library there which presents Kolera’s youngsters with an alternative way of being, a gateway for self-realisation instead of killing time in the gambling den. The novel’s message on Reco is ambivalent. Does he keep his Kolerite identity and enlarge it in a way that includes his new lifestyle and interests? Or does he simply replace his Kolerite identity with another sort of urban identity? Once he moves out, he no longer belongs to Kolera in the way he used to in the past, this is clear. Still, this does not mean that Kolera punishes him because he left the place. Additionally, there are no remarks in the novel indicating that Reco feels himself superior to the Kolera community. At the end of the book, he is the only character in the family who does not have a tragic ending. We do not know the rest of his story, it might well be a positive one, a fact that brings a spark of hope to the work.

zh: 此时，不妨就20世纪70年代末政治化的氛围与阶级斗争，对两部小说略作比较。在《重罗曼》中，身为劳动者的科莱拉人十分显眼。他们不是工厂工人，而是各种手艺师傅门下的学徒。在《垃圾山的故事》中，山民最初大多失业，靠拾荒求生；不过，过了一阵，他们开始在作坊与工厂找到工作。无论科莱拉人还是山民，都不是有阶级意识的无产阶级成员。《垃圾山的故事》与《重罗曼》似乎都以高度政治化的20世纪70年代为背景，激进左翼团体充满马克思主义术语的话语，在两部作品中都作为滑稽因素出现。在《垃圾山的故事》中，泰金展开这一主题，批评左翼无法找到与乡村迁入者相通的语言；卡钱则没有在小说中着力讨论这一点：《重罗曼》中它只出现一次，产生幽默效果，科莱拉的少年们听一群激进分子滔滔不绝地痛斥资本主义剥削时，完全不知所云（Kaçan 1999，62）。然而，在《重罗曼》中，并不是所有科莱拉人都被左翼话语弄糊涂。随着全国的政治两极分化进入街区，一些科莱拉人，如格利的父亲，开始同情左翼。另一方面，花山山民与左翼的关系要棘手得多，上文的分析已详细讨论过。这些主题在两部小说中出现的方式，与它们关于迁入者城市化的不同信息一致。
en: At this point it might be meaningful to make a few comparisons between the two novels as regards the politicised atmosphere of the late 1970s and class struggle. In
, Kolerites who are labourers have high visibility. They are not workers in factories but apprentices under masters of various crafts. In

, the Hill folk are mostly unemployed at the beginning, picking over the garbage to survive; yet, after a while they start finding jobs at workshops and factories. Neither Kolerites nor the Hill folk are class-conscious members of the proletariat. Both
and
seem to be set during the highly politicised era of the 1970s, and the discourse of the radical left groups loaded with Marxist terminology appears as a comic element in both of them. While in
Tekin develops this theme as a criticism of the Left for not being able to find a mutual language with rural migrants, Kaçan does not dwell on this point in his novel: in

it appears only once with a humorous effect, when teenagers of Kolera get completely lost as they are listening to a group of radicals’ tirade about capitalist exploitation (Kaçan 1999, 62). However, in

the leftist discourse does not confuse all Kolerites. As the political polarisation of the country arrives in the neighbourhood, some Kolerites, such as Gıli’s father, develop sympathy for the Left. On the other hand, the Flower Hill folk have a much more problematic relationship with the Left, as discussed in detail in the analysis above. The ways these themes appear in the two novels are in line with their disparate messages in terms of migrants’ urbanisation.

zh: 在《重罗曼》中，我们看到被称为“受敬重的狂欢大姐”（Kaçan 1999，94）的坚强女性；她们在街区中的存在，突出了科莱拉的城市文化。《垃圾山的故事》中没有这样的女性，只有蒂林塔兹·菲丹是例外。事实上，《垃圾山的故事》中的菲丹与《重罗曼》中的美洲狮泽赫拉十分相似；两人都在某一时刻觉得，有责任教育自己街区的女性。然而，她们的使命结束时，受到启发的女人们却面临相反的命运：花山女性接受菲丹的教导后，当她们表达对亲密等方面的期待时，遭到丈夫的敌视；而把泽赫拉奉为导师的科莱拉女性，却开始在某些方面获得与男人平等的对待。虽然这只是科莱拉女性中的一个小群体，卡钱展开这一主题的方式，仍然暗示科莱拉的性别角色内含一种城市所具有的进步潜力。
en: In
we see strong women described as “respectable senior sister revellers” (Kaçan 1999, 94) whose presence in the neighbourhood accentuates the urban culture in Kolera. In
there are no such women, apart from one, Tirintaz Fidan. In fact, Fidan in
and Puma Zehra in

are very similar to each other, as both of them at one point feel a responsibility to educate the women of their neighbourhood. However, at the end of their mission, the women they inspire face quite opposite destinies: the women of Flower Hill enlightened by Fidan’s teaching face the hostility of their husbands when they manifest expectations such as intimacy, while the women of Kolera for whom Zehra becomes a guru start to be treated equally with men in certain respects. This is a small group of Kolerite women, but still, the way Kaçan develops this theme suggests an inherently urban progressive potential in gender roles in Kolera.

zh: 如上文所引，穆拉特·贝尔盖强调，花山是《垃圾山的故事》的主人公（1994a，224）。同样，耶尔德兹·埃杰维特强调，《重罗曼》中的科莱拉街区“几乎像一个会呼吸的有机生命”（2001，215）。不过，在《垃圾山的故事》中，花山是
；在《重罗曼》中，科莱拉则是一个
。《垃圾山的故事》没有英雄，没有作为主人公的人，这强化了花山作为小说主人公的地位；而在《重罗曼》中，尽管科莱拉作为主要人物十分重要，格利才是主人公。与此在某种程度上相呼应，《垃圾山的故事》的读者跟随花山，从第一批棚屋建起之日，一直看到它失宠之日；而《重罗曼》中的科莱拉，则被描绘为一个成熟的街区。
en: Murat Belge, as referred to above, stresses that Flower Hill is the protagonist of
(1994a, 224). Similarly, Yıldız Ecevit emphasises that in
the neighbourhood of Kolera is “almost like an organic being which breathes” (2001, 215). However, while in
Flower Hill is
, in
Kolera is
. In
, there is no hero, no person as protagonist, and this enforces Flower Hill’s position as the protagonist of the novel; while in
, despite Kolera’s significance as a major character, Gıli is the protagonist. Somewhat in line with that, in
the reader follows Flower Hill from the day of the first shanties until the day it falls from grace; while in
Kolera is illustrated as a mature neighbourhood.

zh: 值得记住的是，花山与科莱拉都是受真实街区启发而创造的虚构场景。然而，在《重罗曼》中，多拉普代雷及其毗邻街区对虚构科莱拉的启发直接而明确；《垃圾山的故事》中的花山则并非如此。尽管花山与科莱拉都是迁入者和穷人居住的街区，它们仍有显著差异。花山是远离市中心的棚户区，科莱拉则是市中心的贫困街区。两地的生活方式几乎完全不同。在花山，山民与市中心及其城市氛围相隔绝；而科莱拉人与贝伊奥卢——城市文化艺术与夜生活的心脏——有着极为紧密的联系。科莱拉不同宗教与背景的人毗邻而居，世界主义遗产是生活的核心要素。简单说来，相当数量的科莱拉人已经通过生活方式与观念，获得城市身份；而山民的城市化进程尚未开始。正如下文所论，这些核心差别，是两部小说以不同方式阐释城市权利概念的基础。
en: It can be useful to remember that both Flower Hill and Kolera are fictional settings inspired by actually existing neighbourhoods. However, while in
the inspiration of Dolapdere and adjacent neighbourhoods in the creation of the fictional Kolera is direct and explicit, this is not the case with Flower Hill in

. Although both Flower Hill and Kolera are neighbourhoods where migrants and the poor live, they have considerable differences from each other. Flower Hill is a shanty town away from the city centre, while Kolera is a poor neighbourhood in the centre of the city. The lifestyles experienced in the two places are almost entirely different from each other. In Flower Hill, the Hill folk are isolated from the city centre and its urban atmosphere, while Kolerites have a very close connection with Beyoğlu, the heart of culture and the arts, as well as the nightlife of the city. The cosmopolitan heritage is a central aspect of the life in Kolera where people from various religions and backgrounds live side by side. Put simply, a considerable number of Kolerites have adopted urban identities, with their lifestyles and perceptions, unlike the Hill folk who have yet to start their process of urbanisation. These central differences constitute the basis for the dissimilar elaboration of the concept of the right to the city in the two novels as discussed below.

zh: 两部作品中都有争取地方的斗争。在《垃圾山的故事》中，住房权是斗争的核心：山民为保住自己的棚屋，与国家的力量，也就是拆屋者搏斗。在《重罗曼》中，同样存在争取地方的斗争；这一次，是科莱拉的好人反抗企图统治街区的黑帮的斗争。在前者中，山民被剥夺了能够在城市生活的最低物质条件。在后者中，科莱拉人早已达到这些最低标准：有些贫穷，有些家境尚可，但都有住处。他们在城中的存在，并不限于能够生存，而是超出了这一点。通过格利的生活与内心世界，卡钱描绘了在科莱拉的一种存在方式，接近列斐伏尔所说的“栖居”，即“参与社会生活”（1996，76）。格利把自己的街区、进而把整个伊斯坦布尔视为作品，视为所有居民共同创造的东西。如上所述，他对老建筑的赞赏，恰好表现了这一认识。然而，在《垃圾山的故事》中，城市远远还不是山民在这一意义上栖居的地方，他们只是在努力活下来；与城市更深的联系，尚未进入视野。
en: In both works, there is a fight for place. In
, the right to housing is at the centre of this fight: Hill folk battle against the forces of the state (i.e., demolishers) to be able to stay in their shanties. In

there is a fight for place, too. This one is the fight of the good people of Kolera against the mafia who try to rule the neighbourhood. In the former, Hill folk are deprived of the minimum physical conditions to be able to live in the city. In the latter, Kolerites had long before reached these minimum standards, some of them poor, some of them with moderate means, but they all have a place to live. Their existence in the city is not limited to being able to survive there, it is more than that. Through Gıli’s life and inner world, Kaçan illustrates a way of being in Kolera which is close to what Lefebvre describes as “to inhabit”, that is “to take part in social life” (1996, 76). Gıli perceives his neighbourhood and by extension the whole of Istanbul as an
, as something created by all its inhabitants. His admiration of old buildings is a perfect manifestation of this perception, as discussed above. In
, however, the city is very far from being a place inhabited by the Hill folk in this sense, they simply try to stay alive in it; a deeper connection with the city is not yet on the horizon.

zh: 《垃圾山的故事》没有《重罗曼》中格利那样的人物主人公，这强化了小说的这一信息：城市并不是迁入者能够按照城市语境的匿名性所要求的方式发展身份的地方。他们像在乡村时一样，以共同体方式生活，并不寻求个体化。在《垃圾山的故事》中，共同体精神近似于乡村语境。《重罗曼》中也有共同体；然而，这个共同体的世界主义团结与个体性相容。格利在个体化道路上决定成为比蒂里姆时，只是搬到了街区的赌窟。科莱拉是寻求个体性的合适环境。格利的父亲阿里离开同乡聚居的街区，搬来科莱拉时，也是在朝个体化迈出一步。
en: The absence of a human protagonist in
, such as Gıli in

, reinforces this message of the novel: the city is not a place where migrants can develop their identities in the way the anonymity of the urban context requires. They live as a community, as in the rural context, they are not in search of individualisation. In
, the community soul is akin to the rural context. There is community in
too; however, the cosmopolitan solidarity of this community is compatible with individuality. When Gıli, on the way to individualisation decides to become a

, he simply moves to the gambling den in the neighbourhood. Kolera is the right environment in the search for individuality. When Gıli’s father Ali left the community neighbourhood to live in Kolera, this was also a step towards individualisation.

zh: 两部小说处理被他者化群体的方式有显著差异。在《重罗曼》中，罗姆人创造了科莱拉的声景。他们主要是街区的乐手，却不是同质类别；其中也有窃贼，小说前面两个罗姆男人从阳台偷地毯的段落就表明了这一点。把他们描绘成异质群体，有些从事轻微犯罪，有些作为乐手丰富街区氛围，这是一种否定罗姆人污名化话语的现实主义视角。仅仅真实地描写这些人，就显得富于同情，因为人们实际上对他们的看法是负面的，不仅在土耳其如此，在全球也是如此。《垃圾山的故事》中却出现了这样的歧视性话语：罗姆人开始统治原来的花山后，它就变成了毒品与卖淫的中心。
en: The two novels have considerable differences as regards their ways of addressing the otherised groups. In

the Romani people create the soundscape of Kolera. They are primarily the musicians of the neighbourhood, yet they are not a homogeneous category; there are also thieves among them, as we see in an early passage where two Romani men steal carpets from balconies. Their portrayal as a heterogeneous category, some as petty criminals others as musicians enriching the atmosphere of their neighbourhood, is a realistic perspective that negates the stigmatising discourse against the Romani people. Being simply realistic about these people sounds sympathetic because the de facto perception of them is negative, not only in Turkey but globally. Such discriminatory discourse appears in
when the former Çiçektepe becomes a centre of drugs and prostitution after the Romani people start ruling the place.

zh: 在少数群体问题上，卡钱通过《重罗曼》的人物、故事和叙述声音，不带怀旧地赞美伊斯坦布尔的非穆斯林居民，把他们视为城市世界主义肌理的核心要素；而《垃圾山的故事》只用一个人物来表现少数群体：伊扎克先生，他极有可能是犹太人，被描绘为贪婪的厂主。《重罗曼》没有提及阿列维派；而在《垃圾山的故事》中，如上所述，对他们的描写略带歧视。两部作品处理毒品与卖淫的方式也相当不同。在《垃圾山的故事》中，泰金只把参与这些“活动”的人描绘为堕落的象征；而在《重罗曼》中，卡钱避免把他们描绘为同质类别，呈现了涉足毒品与卖淫的正面人物和负面人物。
en: When it comes to minorities, with
’s characters, story and narrative voice Kaçan praises, without nostalgia, the non-Muslim inhabitants of Istanbul as a central aspect of the cosmopolitan fabric of the city, whereas in
, minorities are presented with only one character: Mr Izak, who is most probably Jewish and is portrayed as a greedy factory owner. There is no reference to Alevis in
, while in
, as discussed above, their portrayal is slightly on the discriminatory side. The two works are also quite dissimilar regarding the way they address drugs and prostitution. While in
, Tekin portrays those involved in such ‘activities’ solely as symbols of degeneration, in
, Kaçan refrains from depicting them as a homogeneous category, and presents both negative and positive characters involved with drugs and prostitution.

zh: 两部小说看待城市性可能性的差异，与它们处理城市权利概念的方式相一致。在《垃圾山的故事》中，努力弄懂城市环境的迁入者，从城市权利的角度，为物质生活必需品而斗争；而在《重罗曼》中，城市权利意味着栖居城市、把城市作为作品来体验的权利。总之，两部作品都让叙述者使用具有本真性的语言，从而取消城市叙述者相对于迁入者人物的优越地位，在这一点上相似；但它们关于争取城市权利的斗争，以及获得城市身份的过程，传达了不同的信息。
en: The differences in the approaches of the two novels to the possibilities of urbanity are in line with the way they address the concept of the right to the city. In
, migrants who are trying to figure out the urban context are fighting for the material necessities in terms of the right to the city, whereas in
, the right to the city means the right to inhabit the city, to experience the city as

. In short, while the two works are similar in their use of an authentic language by the narrator, therefore abolishing the superiority of an urban narrator over migrant characters, they convey distinct messages about the struggle for the right to the city and the process of adopting an urban identity.
